_alternateNames: Entity resolution, added 11 August 2026. The site spelled the name ONLY as 'Mohamed Fat-hy' — the hyphenated form appeared in every field and the unhyphenated 'Fathy' appeared nowhere outside the LinkedIn and GitHub URL slugs. But 'Mohamed Fathy' is how most people type it, including anyone who heard the name spoken rather than read it, and a search for it returns nine other software engineers of the same name plus a competing developer portfolio at mohamedfathy.dev. These variants are emitted as schema.org alternateName so Google and LLMs can resolve all three spellings to one person. Order matters: the canonical spelling leads.
summary: I build apps and the systems that run them — phone apps, websites, and the servers behind them. Products run in 10 markets across four continents, from Egypt and Saudi Arabia to South Korea and the USA.
_markets: The real client footprint, confirmed by Mohamed on 11 August 2026 — NOT derived from projects.json, which lists only the 8 documented case studies out of 15+ delivered. The European Union is a bloc, not a country: it is kept last and typed as an AdministrativeArea in the JSON-LD so the schema stays literally correct. Never write '10 countries' anywhere — the honest phrasing is '10 markets'.
_copyLayers: hero.* is Layer 1 (plain language, no jargon — a non-technical, non-native English reader must understand it in one pass). hero.gloss is Layer 2: it names the technical terms and immediately says what they mean, so search engines and LLMs get the keywords without the human having to decode them. Layer 3 (full technical vocabulary) lives in JSON-LD, llms.txt, and the project detail pages. Do not move Layer 3 words up into hero.headline or hero.body.

hero._proof: Ordered strongest-first for a warm visitor whose real question is 'will this go wrong for me?'. Repeat business answers that better than any count, and it is the one claim a competitor cannot copy — two clients in testimonials.json hired Mohamed twice, one saying so explicitly. Project count and download numbers are deliberately NOT here: volume is a vanity axis and Mohamed asked not to open with either. Both live lower down and in the machine layer instead.
hero._tech: Visible copy, so it is kept SHORT on purpose — a long technology list reads junior and dilutes the AI direction into one item among many. It names only what Mohamed wants to be hired for, AI first. .NET, Node.js, Firebase, SQL/NoSQL and the rest are all still carried in knowsAbout and llms.txt, where breadth costs nothing because no human is judging the length. Do not grow this line to cover a technology; grow the machine layer instead.

about: I started my professional journey in Civil Engineering, which built my foundation in analytical thinking and rapid problem-solving.
Transitioning into software engineering taught me to be a 'polyglot' developer—focusing on architectural patterns that apply across any language or framework.
With 5+ years of experience, I specialize in bridging the gap between mobile frontends and complex backends, delivering production apps used across multiple countries.
I thrive on technical variety: architecting clean mobile apps in Flutter, building enterprise service layers in Spring Boot and .NET, and deploying agile, cloud-native logic with JavaScript.
I am heavily focused on Generative AI, using tools like Spring AI to build intelligent, data-driven features into the product core while leveraging AI to accelerate my own engineering lifecycle.
Having served as a Tech Lead, I am an ownership-driven teammate who manages feature delivery end-to-end. I am highly adaptable and open to relocation for the right opportunity.
